speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have multiple skin lesions; can you describe when they first appeared and if they are itchy, painful, or changing in size?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-year-old female. The patient's mother reports noticing multiple painless, nonpruritic papules on the child's abdomen. The child attends daycare where another child was reported to have similar lesions recently. Patient's brother had chickenpox one month ago. Immunizations are up-to-date.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Molluscum Contagiosum. The clinical presentation of multiple, painless, non-pruritic papules in a daycare-aged child with recent exposure to a similar case is highly characteristic of this viral skin infection. I recommend a visual confirmation via dermoscopy if the lesions are atypical, but the diagnosis is likely confirmed based on your description. Is there any family history of immune deficiencies?
